legend.name: Producers
legend.meaning: Make their own food from sunlight

legend.name: Eat producers
legend.meaning: Consumers that eat plants in this web

legend.name: Eat consumers
legend.meaning: Consumers that eat other animals in this web

steps.title: Producers
steps.instruction: Trace the boxes around the oak tree and the berry bush.

note.text: Producers make their own food from sunlight, air and water. Every food web starts with them.

steps.title: Plant eaters
steps.instruction: Trace the boxes around the caterpillar, mouse and rabbit.

note.text: Many caterpillars feed on oaks, mice eat acorns, and rabbits eat leaves and berries. They're consumers.

steps.title: Predators
steps.instruction: Trace the boxes around the chickadee, owl and fox.

note.text: These consumers eat other animals. Chickadees feed caterpillars to their chicks. Owls and foxes hunt mice and rabbits.

steps.title: Arrows from plants
steps.instruction: Draw the three arrows from the plants up to the animals that eat them.

note.text: Each arrow points from the food to the eater. It shows which way matter and energy move.

steps.title: Arrows from animals
steps.instruction: Draw the five arrows to the chickadee, owl and fox.

note.text: The mouse has two arrows leaving it: owls and foxes both eat mice. Linked food chains like this make a food web.
note.remember: Many linked chains = a food web.

steps.title: Color
steps.instruction: Color each group: producers, animals that eat producers, and animals that eat other animals.

steps.title: Read the web
steps.question: In this web, which animals eat the mouse?

options.feedback: Yes. Two arrows leave the mouse: one to the owl, one to the fox.
The arrow goes from the oak to the mouse: the mouse eats acorns, not the other way round.
No arrow joins the mouse to the chickadee. Follow the mouse's arrows: owl and fox.
Rabbits eat plants. The mouse's arrows go to the owl and the fox.

steps.title: Predict
steps.question: A disease kills most of the owls. What would probably happen to the mice, at first?

options.text: There would be more mice, because fewer are eaten
options.feedback: Right. With fewer owls hunting them, more mice survive. A change to one living thing ripples through the web.
Owls eat mice. Fewer owls means fewer mice get eaten, so mice would increase.
Everything in a web is linked. Fewer owls means more mice survive.

options.text: The mice would start eating owls
options.feedback: Mice eat acorns in this web. With fewer owls hunting them, more mice survive.

steps.title: Energy
steps.question: The fox gets energy by eating a rabbit. Where did that energy first come from?

options.text: The sun, through the berry bush
options.feedback: Yes. The bush stored the sun's energy, the rabbit ate its leaves and berries, and the fox ate the rabbit.
No arrow joins the owl and the fox. Follow the fox's arrows back: rabbit, bush, sun.
No arrow joins the oak and the rabbit. The rabbit ate the berry bush, which got its energy from the sun.
Animals get energy from food. Follow it back: rabbit, bush, sun.
